model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves of six different model configurations over the course of training iterations. The x-axis represents the number of iterations (#Iteration), displayed on a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents Loss, also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model variant. The Vanilla line, shown in light purple (solid), starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations before gradually leveling off, reaching approximately 2.62 by 140,000 iterations. The StrmLLM (n=64) line, shown in blue (solid), follows a similar initial steep decline but settles at a noticeably higher loss, ending at approximately 2.63–2.65 near 140,000 iterations, remaining consistently above most other lines throughout training. The SepLLM (n=64) line, shown in orange (solid), starts similarly near 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.52–2.53 by 140,000 iterations, tracking below the Vanilla and StrmLLM lines for most of the training. The SepLLM (n=64, H) line, shown in green (solid), follows a very similar trajectory to the orange SepLLM (n=64) line, ending at approximately 2.51–2.52. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) line, shown in red (solid), also closely overlaps with the orange and green lines, reaching approximately 2.50–2.52 by 140,000 iterations. The SepLLM (n=128) line, shown in dark blue/navy (solid), follows a trajectory that is slightly above the other SepLLM variants but below the Vanilla and StrmLLM lines, ending at approximately 2.55–2.57 by 140,000 iterations. All lines exhibit a rapid decrease in loss during the first approximately 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows considerably, with the curves flattening toward the right side of the plot. Shaded regions around several of the lines suggest variability or confidence intervals.
